items.title: v2.1.331
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v2.1.331](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.331)** — _Claude Code releases_. — Code Mode now runs in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS.
  - Added an API connectivity section to `claude doctor` that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error
  - Fixed MCP tool calls hanging for up to 30 minutes on some malformed replies from a local or WebSocket server
  - Added `optionalDependencies` to plugin manifests: plugins that install with the plugin listing them and can be disabled or uninstalled on their own

- 🛠 **[0.172.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.172.0)** — _Codex releases_. — Codex 0.172.0 adds thread links, slash-command Tab completion and task-group navigation to the terminal CLI.
  - Follow thread links from search results and transcripts to open saved conversations and nested agents
  - `Tab` completes arguments for supported slash commands, e.g. `/mcp lo` to `/mcp login`
  - `Shift+Up` and `Shift+Down` jump between task groups in the agent command center
  - `codex exec resume` restores saved sandbox permissions, working directory and workspace roots

items.title: v2.4.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v2.4.0](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.4.0)** — _OpenCode releases_. — OpenCode 2.4.0 gives the desktop app a built-in browser and timer- or cron-driven automations.
  - Imports sign-ins and browsing history from Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, plus extensions from Chromium stores
  - The agent can read and drive the same pages without switching apps
  - Automations run a prompt, script or shell command on a timer, cron schedule or MCP event
  - The image tool is now `generate_image`; old permission rules map automatically

items.title: Hermes Agent canary canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[Hermes Agent canary canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3)** — _Hermes Agent releases_. — The November 23 Hermes canary build is mostly plugin-catalog additions plus release-pipeline wiring.
  - New catalog entries include beeper-platform, utcp-bridge, valetudo, deny-record and katara memory
  - `stable-release.yml` now wires commit claims in with read-only native legs
  - macOS arm64 DMG and both Windows MSIX builds passed install smoke tests

items.title: v1.44.0
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[v1.44.0](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/releases/tag/v1.44.0)** — _OpenHands releases_. — OpenHands 1.44.0 adds per-audience automation visibility and an editable key-value store for automations.
  - Conversation mentions ship behind the `conversation_mentions` flag
  - A Factories sidebar entry adds list and drill-in views
  - Hitting a budget now shows a readable error instead of failing opaquely
  - `agent-server` requirement moves to 1.63.1

items.title: Release v0.28.4
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[Release v0.28.4](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/tag/v0.28.4)** — _Qwen Code releases_. — Qwen Code 0.28.4 adds built-in Gemini 4 reasoning defaults and a workspace artifact library in local daemon mode.
  - Artifact library scans the workspace progressively and streams updates
  - Web Shell chat gains a shared ChatSurface, Continue badges and suggestion chips
  - Local Runtime creates its state directory at spawn with owner-private permissions

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/23/anthropic-launches-claude-ship-letting-ai-agents-review-fix-and-approve-code-changes/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Anthropic is automating the step after code generation: Claude can now approve a pull request, not just write it.
  - Code Review is already generally available; PR Steward and Claude Approvals are still beta
  - PR Steward fixes failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review feedback
  - Approval rules live as a natural-language policy file inside the repository

items.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation](https://allenai.org/blog/robotrack)** — _Ai2 blog_. — The best point trackers lose 3.0 to 6.6 AJ when Ai2 scores them on real robot footage instead of RoboTAP.
  - CoWTracker drops from 70.5 to 63.9 on the 307-video RoboTrack-Bench
  - RoboTracker-Warp, retrained on synthetic data, recovers 2.1 AJ to 66.0
  - A pipetting test finished 17 of 20 trials versus 8 for object masks

items.title: Google workers tell their employer not to punish schools that don't want AI
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Google workers tell their employer not to punish schools that don't want AI](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/11/google-alphabet-union-school-ai-protest-gemini-workers-petition/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Hundreds of Google staff want their employer to stop tying school Search access to Gemini adoption.
  - The Alphabet Workers Union petition asks Sundar Pichai to retract the policy
  - Schools that switch off Gemini lose Search access starting next year
  - New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago are discussing alternative search engines

items.title: Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy](https://the-decoder.com/anthropics-appetite-for-compute-is-pushing-xai-toward-a-rent-over-build-strategy/)** — _The Decoder_. — xAI is turning into a GPU landlord: Anthropic now pays it roughly $3.1 billion a month, with Google at $800 million.
  - Either contract can be canceled with 90 days' notice
  - Musk pushed engineers in August for more revenue per GPU
  - The 60-person Grok Imagine team was told in November it would be disbanded

items.title: Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model](https://the-decoder.com/z-ai-follows-openai-into-loop-transformer-territory-with-its-new-750b-flagship-model/)** — _The Decoder_. — Z.ai retrained its GLM-5 base into a loop model, running 28 layers twice, as OpenAI has since GPT-6 Astra.
  - It claims 750B parameters perform like 2 to 3 trillion
  - Benchmarks so far come only from a 30B test model
  - AIME25 rose 19.2 to 30.4 in that test; GPQA-Diamond 47.6 to 56.3
  - Weights promised after safety testing; token pricing not announced

items.title: Google Cloud CISO talks agentic AI security and the future of the SOC
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Google Cloud CISO talks agentic AI security and the future of the SOC](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/24/chris-betz-google-agentic-ai-security/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Chris Betz says human reaction time is no longer a viable defense baseline.
  - Attackers now compress six months of reconnaissance into hours
  - The future alert is a verified conclusion, not a raw ticket
  - Juniors move up to doctrine, risk appetite and verifying agent actions
  - Boards should ask if every agent action can be traced and reversed

items.title: Xalgorix: Open-source AI penetration testing tool
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Xalgorix: Open-source AI penetration testing tool](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/23/xalgorix-ai-penetration-testing-tool/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Xalgorix is an Apache-2.0 pen-testing agent whose verifier must re-exploit every finding before the report ships.
  - It drives Nmap, Nuclei and SQLmap through a 22-phase test plan
  - A scope guard blocks any host outside the configured targets
  - The verifier gets read-only tools, eight turns and three minutes per check
  - Claude Opus 5.5 gave the best results, but no benchmarks are published

items.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1038390/signal-blocking-ai-agent-screenshots-mobile-app)** — _The Verge AI_. — Signal now blocks screenshots on Android and iOS to keep Siri and Gemini out of your chats, a fix it calls incomplete.
  - Users can re-enable screenshots, at the cost of Signal's privacy guarantees
  - Whittaker says the block misses file-system access and cannot be done on macOS
  - Signal wants Apple, Google and Microsoft to give developers agent-access controls

items.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/20/1149399/the-most-misunderstood-graph-in-ai-just-got-a-major-update/)** — _MIT Tech Review AI_. — METR's much-misread time-horizon graph now includes fuzzier work, and models fell short of humans there.
  - Not one AI-designed evaluation was good enough for METR staff to use
  - Models also trailed humans at scoring philosophical arguments
  - Opus 5.5 now lands borderline above the bar; a year ago everything was clearly below

items.title: v0.34.1rc0: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM100 TP=2 and TP=8 skinny GEMM plans (#69529)
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[v0.34.1rc0: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM100 TP=2 and TP=8 skinny GEMM plans (#69529)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.34.1rc0)** — _vLLM releases_. — Blackwell perf work keeps landing as perf-only tags: this one adds SM100 skinny GEMM plans for Qwen4Exp at tensor parallelism 2 and 8.
  - Same corner as last week's FlashInfer top-k swap, 1.30-2.25x faster long-context decode on GB300
  - Release notes carry the commit and sign-off only, no benchmark figures yet

items.title: Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory](https://github.com/ShinMegamiBoson/lookatmyquant)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — A third-party quantiser squeezed Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini into a 5.4 GB build.
  - LookAtMyQuant is MIT-licensed and gives more bits to the parts that matter most
  - The small build beats a larger Unsloth version on GSM8K and HumanEval
  - Runs on an Apple M5 Max, even though the vendor suggests about 20 GB

items.title: Qwen4 Max is live on Together AI
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Qwen4 Max is live on Together AI](https://www.together.ai/blog/qwen4-max)** — _Together AI blog_. — Together put Alibaba's 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen4 Max on serverless inference with a 1M-token window, 30% off until Nov 22.
  - Its first test: 344 Tornado files, 652,519 tokens, one patch that passed the maintainers' tests
  - The request cost 69 cents; a cached repeat ran about 3 cents
  - Streaming is mandatory and thinking is on by default, billed as output

items.title: 12 Rules for a Software Factory That Doesn't Ship Slop — Dex Horthy, Factory
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [12 Rules for a Software Factory That Doesn't Ship Slop — Dex Horthy, Factory](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-NFMsM2y0Vk) — **AI Engineer** (20m24s). — Dex Horthy argues the best model still scores about 16% on Slop Code Bench, which tracks how well agents evolve a codebase over time. - 12 practices, from forward and back pressure to planning and lint rules against slop - Launches an Anti-Slop Manifesto at slopmanifesto.com - Closes on why reviewing agent work still matters

items.title: Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil](https://youtube.com/watch?v=JNexz3Tbiu8) — **AI Engineer** (19m56s). — Human attention, not model capability, is the limit: build the workshop before the software factory. - Pi's core tools are unchanged after a year; the models got better - Tasks now run 14 minutes instead of two and a half - 141 projects started, only 10 to 15 kept alive - Executive summaries instead of reading code

items.title: A Murder of MCP Servers Taming AI Tool Sprawl with GraphQL Federation and a Knowledge Graph
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [A Murder of MCP Servers Taming AI Tool Sprawl with GraphQL Federation and a Knowledge Graph](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HPMGxK81zO0) — **Neo4j** (25m27s). — For teams drowning in per-vendor MCP auth: federate Linear, Slack and Neo4j behind one endpoint. - GraphQL federation replaces per-server auth and disconnected tool namespaces - Persisted operations govern which calls an agent is allowed to make - Neo4j models Linear issues and Slack threads as nodes with typed edges - Closing demo answers a question none of the three systems could alone

items.title: Harness Adapters - Train Your Model to Your Harness
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Harness Adapters - Train Your Model to Your Harness](https://youtube.com/watch?v=4nnFw0TPDKM) — **Sam Witteveen** (16m23s). — For anyone tuning a small open model: adapt the model to the harness, not the other way around. - LoRA adapters for Qwen3.8-27B, one each for Pi, Hermes Agent and OpenCode - Training happens inside the real harness; a super-adapter then spans them - Reported payoff is a higher score on half the tokens

items.title: AI Writes 44% More Code. So Why Isn't More Software Shipping?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [AI Writes 44% More Code. So Why Isn't More Software Shipping?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cI1WVdTpFZY) — **DopeShit** (9m12s). — Harvard tracked 720,542 workers at 655 companies: 44% more code written, only ~14% more finished work. - Time to merge rose 56% and review comments rose 39% - Letting AI review the code has not fixed the review line - The same pattern appears in hospitals with AI scribes - Two simulated futures for 2031, and what they mean for developers

items.title: My AI Coding Agent Broke a Rule, Then Rewrote CLAUDE.md
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [My AI Coding Agent Broke a Rule, Then Rewrote CLAUDE.md](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DGw2ObWdP1c) — **Sebastian Buzdugan** (9m25s). — Candid, sponsor-funded test of whether a rules service actually stops agents bending instruction files. - Qodo turned instruction files across 13 repos into 361 structured rules - Hand audit of 69 rules: 50 faithful, 8 over-hardened, 6 misread - Get Rules prevented one of 8 rule-break attempts; each task ran once - Imported rules also blocked one valid fix and overrode one request

items.title: I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model](https://youtube.com/watch?v=YNal-nlQ5F8) — **James Briggs** (33m16s). — A 436M-parameter local model beats Jev on routing accuracy, calibration, latency and cost in one workspace. - Picks the right agent on 85.9% of 205 test posts against Jev's 78.0% - Calibration error 0.052 versus 0.071, at ~27 ms per decision on an RTX 5000 Ada - Under 0.1¢ per 1K decisions on an M4 Max against Jev's 5¢

items.title: This Opensource Repo Actually saves upto 98% USAGE across Codex,Claude & More!?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [This Opensource Repo Actually saves upto 98% USAGE across Codex,Claude & More!?](https://youtube.com/watch?v=aFmu4rLgH8U) — **AICodeKing** (8m46s). — Worth trying only if your agent sits on Gemini 4 or an original Fable 5 model. - MIT-licensed, around 7,600 stars; renders bulky context as 5x8 pixel PNG pages - 48,000 characters of prompt and tool docs fall from about 25,000 tokens to 2,700 - Measured 59% to 70% lower end-to-end bill; the Claude Code demo went from $42 to $6 - Sonnet 5.5 read 2 of 15 test hex IDs, so skip imaging it

items.title: MCP Registry: The App Store for AI Agent Tools
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [MCP Registry: The App Store for AI Agent Tools](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er0ay2ecHw8) — **Kernel Cast** (2m15s). — For anyone new to MCP: a 2m15s map of the registry agents query to find tool servers. - Entries are `server.json` records pointing at npm, PyPI or OCI packages, or remote URLs - Framed as an App Store for agent tools, spanning GitHub, databases and search

items.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[Ladybird's first alpha release](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/23/ladybird/)** — _Simon Willison_. — Simon Willison installed Ladybird's first alpha without compiling it and calls the result very impressive. He still will not sign into GitHub or Gmail with it.

items.title: If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it](https://cekrem.github.io/posts/if-you-stop-writing-code-you-also-get-worse-at-reviewing-it/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Christian Ekrem argues that delegating all coding atrophies the review skill, since judging code depends on having written it.
  - Keep practicing, he says; reading AI output is not practice

items.title: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[[AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft](https://latent.space/p/ainews-jensen-is-back-and-openai-shows-its-pretraining-curve-joined-by-microsoft/)** — _Latent Space (swyx)_. — OpenAI published its pretraining loss curve and proposed labs agree on a shared development limit.
  - Perplexity went from about 0.99 on GPT-3.5 to 0.76 on GPT6 Astra
  - Pachocki expects the next capability jump around 0.68-0.70
  - Microsoft cosigned, reporting MAI-2 Base at 0.819 on the same eval set
  - Separately, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO eleven days after his resignation

items.title: Fast-Anything: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Fast-Anything: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow](https://github.com/EL4CTEO/fast-anything)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — EL4CTEO's fast-anything ports only an app's slowest functions to Rust, then replays recorded calls before enabling each port.
  - port records up to 500 real calls and builds a one-function Rust crate
  - Python fuzzy dedupe went from 4.91s to 42ms, 116x faster

items.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
items.bullet_md: - 🧪 **[Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.29897)** — _HF Daily Papers_. — Motion Mamba 2.0 swaps bounded attention caches for a Mamba backbone so humanoid controllers keep distant history without paying repeated denoising.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[Perplexity and Intelligence](https://openai.com/index/perplexity-and-intelligence)** — _OpenAI blog_. — Jakub Pachocki argues perplexity should be the shared cross-lab yardstick, and proposes common limits labs commit not to cross.
  - OpenAI published numbers on a fixed internal-code set: GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91
  - Capabilities emerged below 0.8, with math breakthroughs at ~0.76
  - He expects the next transformative window around 0.68-0.7 log-perplexity

items.title: The effective end of easy distillation from OpenAI and Anthropic models may be…
items.bullet_md:
- 🦋 **[The effective end of easy distillation from OpenAI and Anthropic models may be…](https://bsky.app/profile/emollick.bsky.social/post/3n2req7quy225)** — _@emollick.bsky.social on Bluesky_. — Ethan Mollick suggests easy distillation ending may sit behind the relative slowdown in open weights progress.
  - OpenAI reports protected-reasoning extraction success falling from 54.0% to 0.2% on GPT-6.2 Astra

items.title: On Dwarkesh Patel’s November 2026 Podcast With Paul Christiano
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[On Dwarkesh Patel’s November 2026 Podcast With Paul Christiano](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/on-dwarkesh-patels-november-2026)** — _Don't Worry About the Vase (Zvi)_. — Zvi annotates Christiano's Dwarkesh appearance, where Christiano puts roughly 1-in-3 odds on superintelligence within a year if nothing slows.
  - Puts loss-of-control risk above 10% over the next year alone
  - Urges labs to pause algorithmic progress until security catches up

items.title: Riemann Hypothesis may have been solved with the help of Claude.
items.bullet_md:
- 🦋 **[Riemann Hypothesis may have been solved with the help of Claude.](https://bsky.app/profile/emollick.bsky.social/post/3n2qvqp4fts2e)** — _@emollick.bsky.social on Bluesky_. — Ethan Mollick flags Levent Alpöge's claimed Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, posted in Lean.
  - Alpöge says the method extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
  - The proof has not yet been verified independently

items.title: Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux (11 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux (11 minute read)](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/application-development/lessons-from-building-sashiko-an-agentic-code-review-system)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — Google detailed Sashiko, its open-source Gemini code reviewer for Linux kernel patches.
  - Up to seven specialist sessions run in parallel, each on one bug class
  - About 1,200 reviews a day across more than 100 kernel mailing lists
  - 60-day post-merge fix rate fell to 2.2% in Linux 7.2
  - Sashiko is credited in 2,000+ mainline commits and 528 of 2026's kernel CVEs

items.title: Google books a dedicated New Glenn launch in Q1 2029 for Project Suncatcher, its orbital TPU compute constellation (1…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Google books a dedicated New Glenn launch in Q1 2029 for Project Suncatcher, its orbital TPU compute constellation (1…](https://www.blueorigin.com/news/google-selects-new-glenn-for-project-suncatcher)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — Google booked a dedicated New Glenn launch for Q1 2029 to put Project Suncatcher satellites in sun-synchronous orbit.
  - Each satellite carries roughly a data center rack's worth of compute capacity
  - Follows an October test that booted TPUs in orbit and sent a Gemma 4 haiku home

items.title: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China (2…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China (2…](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/nvidia-california-bonta-subpoena-china-chips.html)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — California's attorney general subpoenaed Nvidia over whether advanced chips or confidential data reached China.
  - Rob Bonta also asks whether Nvidia misled investors and the public
  - The subpoena follows Jensen Huang's resignation over an alleged affair
  - Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, is a suspected Chinese spy
  - Nvidia shares are down 22% in the nine trading days since

items.title: Detachable fiber connectors are emerging for CPO and NPO because standard fibers can't be reworked, tray-handled, or…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Detachable fiber connectors are emerging for CPO and NPO because standard fibers can't be reworked, tray-handled, or…](https://semiengineering.com/detachable-fiber-connectors-pose-new-challenges-for-photonics)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — Semiconductor Engineering surveys why co-packaged and near-packaged optics need detachable fiber connectors, with no standard interface yet.
  - Pigtails break tray handling, so Amkor and Senko favor detachable parts
  - Senko demonstrated 10,000 matings with little variation in insertion loss
  - At 125 µm with cladding, 16 fibers eat scarce shoreline real estate

items.title: Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports network calls (1 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports network calls (1 minute read)](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/cloudfront-functions-network-calls/)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — CloudFront Functions can now call APIs mid-request via cf.fetch(), removing the Lambda@Edge detour for data-dependent edge logic.
  - cf.beacon() sends analytics events in the background without slowing viewers, even for cached content
  - Priced at $0.10 per million network calls on top of invocation charges
  - Included at no extra cost in CloudFront flat-rate Pro plan and above

items.title: Nvidia expands Azure infrastructure and on-premises AI options (5 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Nvidia expands Azure infrastructure and on-premises AI options (5 minute read)](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/microsoft-ignite-accelerated-computing-azure-windows-pcs)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — Nvidia used Ignite to put Vera Rubin NVL72 systems into Azure data centers and push Nemotron 3.5 into Foundry.
  - Azure Local gains Nemotron 3.5 in Foundry Local plus RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs from hardware partners
  - EY adapted Nemotron for purchasing records: 55% better accuracy, 15x lower cost than frontier models
  - Azure Local also adds Jetson Thor and Orin for machine vision and robotics

items.title: Introducing agent controls: An enterprise control plane for agent behavior (10 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Introducing agent controls: An enterprise control plane for agent behavior (10 minute read)](https://commandline.microsoft.com/introducing-agent-controls-an-enterprise-control-plane-for-agent-behavior/)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — Microsoft's agent controls is a managed Azure service that rules on agent actions at runtime, now in public preview.
  - Built on the open-source Agent Control Specification and Agent Hooks
  - Returns allow, deny, or transform, with a receipt naming the policy versions applied
  - Policies mix Content Safety classifiers, LLM judges, and Rego rules

items.title: OVHcloud announces 55 cloud and AI products (5 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[OVHcloud announces 55 cloud and AI products (5 minute read)](https://www.cloudcomputing-news.net/news/ovhcloud-cloud-ai-products-europe-sovereignty/)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — OVHcloud unveiled 55 cloud and AI products at its Paris summit, leaning on European hosting as the differentiator.
  - Plans Nvidia RTX 6000 Pro, Blackwell B300 and Rubin R200 GPUs on bare metal and public cloud
  - OVHai Workspace alpha is free with 5GB per user, data kept in Europe
  - Its Olala mini 7A1B model ships under Apache 2.0 with weights and AI Act documentation

items.title: Ideogram 4.6
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Ideogram 4.6](https://ideogram.ai/models/4.6?_bhlid=69e5fb959782af20bfd5f9ffad282934d9c35d86)** — _The Rundown AI · Nov 20_. — Ideogram 4.6 generates and edits in native 4K, scoring 1,892 on Rapidata's multi-step image edit leaderboard.
  - Ranks above Ideogram 4.5 at 1,866 on the same leaderboard
  - Character consistency rose to 85% from 69% on 4.5
  - API pricing for 4K Precise Edit at High quality is $0.60 per image
